RoB 2.reference: Sterne JAC et al. BMJ 2019;366:l4898. Cochrane Handbook Ch 8.

domains.name: D1: Randomization process
signaling_questions: Was allocation sequence random?
Was allocation sequence concealed until participants recruited and assigned?
Were there baseline imbalances suggesting problems with randomization?

domains.name: D2: Deviations from intended interventions
signaling_questions: Were participants aware of their assigned intervention during the trial?
Were carers and trial personnel aware of participants' assigned intervention?
Were there deviations from intended intervention due to trial context?
Were these deviations likely to impact outcome?
Was an analysis appropriate to estimate the effect of assignment to intervention?

domains.name: D3: Missing outcome data
signaling_questions: Were data for this outcome available for all, or nearly all, participants randomized?
Were there no or small differences in amount of missing data across groups?
Were missing data reasons unrelated to outcome?
Were there no imbalances in missing data across groups?

domains.name: D4: Measurement of outcome
signaling_questions: Was method of measuring outcome appropriate?
Could measurement or ascertainment of outcome differ between groups?
Were outcome assessors aware of intervention received?
Were assessors blinded (for subjective outcomes)?

domains.name: D5: Selection of reported result
signaling_questions: Were data in accordance with pre-specified analysis plan?
Is the reported effect estimate unlikely to be selected from multiple analyses?
Was trial registered before recruitment started?

RoB 2.overall_algorithm: Highest domain risk → overall (with D1/D3 able to downgrade alone).

ROBINS-I.indication: Non-randomized studies of interventions (cohort, case-control, controlled before-after)
ROBINS-I.reference: Sterne JAC et al. Ann Intern Med 2016. Cochrane Handbook Ch 25.

domains.name: D1: Bias due to confounding
signaling_questions: Was confounding modeled appropriately?
Did the authors use appropriate method to control for confounding?
Were all important confounders measured?

domains.name: D2: Bias in selection of participants
signaling_questions: Was selection of participants into the study (or analysis) inappropriate?
Were start of follow-up and start of intervention the same for all participants?

domains.name: D3: Bias in classification of interventions
signaling_questions: Were intervention groups clearly defined?
Could classification of intervention status have been affected by knowledge of outcome?

domains.name: D4: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
signaling_questions: Were there deviations from intended interventions beyond what would be expected?
Were these deviations imbalanced across groups and related to outcomes?

domains.name: D5: Bias due to missing data
signaling_questions: Were outcome data reasonably complete?
Was loss-to-follow-up imbalanced across groups?

domains.name: D6: Bias in measurement of outcomes
signaling_questions: Could outcome measure have been influenced by intervention knowledge?
Were outcome assessors blinded?

domains.name: D7: Bias in selection of the reported result
signaling_questions: Is the reported estimate selected from multiple measurements or analyses?
Was protocol pre-registered?

ROBINS-I.overall_algorithm: Highest domain risk → overall. D1 alone can reach Critical.

QUADAS-2.reference: Whiting PF et al. Ann Intern Med 2011;155:529-536.

domains.name: Patient selection
signaling_questions: Was consecutive/random sampling used?
Was case-control design avoided?
Were inappropriate exclusions avoided?

domains.name: Index test
signaling_questions: Were index test results interpreted without knowledge of reference standard?
Was pre-specified threshold used?

domains.name: Reference standard
signaling_questions: Is reference standard likely to correctly classify target condition?
Were reference standard results interpreted without index test knowledge?

domains.name: Flow and timing
signaling_questions: Was there appropriate interval between index test and reference standard?
Did all patients receive same reference standard?
Were all patients included in analysis?

domains.name: Comparability (max 2 stars)
items: Comparability based on design/control for most important factor

domains.name: Outcome (cohort, max 3 stars) / Exposure (case-control, max 3 stars)

PROBAST.reference: Moons KGM et al. Ann Intern Med 2019;170:51-58. 20 signaling questions across 4 domains; each domain judged for risk of bias AND applicability.

domains.name: participants
signaling_questions: Were appropriate data sources used?
Were participants in the data source appropriate for the review question?

domains.name: predictors
signaling_questions: Were predictors defined and assessed appropriately?

domains.name: outcome
signaling_questions: Was the outcome defined and determined appropriately?

domains.name: analysis
signaling_questions: Were there a reasonable amount of data unavailable? Were missing data handled appropriately?
Was the analysis appropriate given the study design?
Were complex/overfitted models evaluated sensibly?

PROBAST.note: Domain names verified from two independent sources 2026-08-14 ('participants, predictors, outcome, and analysis'). Signaling questions here are SUMMARIES, not verbatim PROBAST items — consult probast.org for the official instrument.

ROBINS-E.reference: ROBINS-E = Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies - of Exposures; 7 bias domains via signaling questions (verified count, 2026-08-14). Critical appraisal: Bero L et al. Syst Rev 2018;7(1) doi:10.1186/s13643-018-0915-2.
ROBINS-E.note: Seven domains confirmed (count verified 2026-08-14 via multiple sources); domain NAMES not yet verified against the official instrument in this environment — deliberately left empty rather than guessed (anti-fabrication). Fetch riskofbias.info and fill before use.
